notes: A raw netcat shell has no job control, no tab completion, and Ctrl+C kills the connection. After spawning a PTY with Python/script, background it (Ctrl+Z), run 'stty raw -echo; fg', then 'reset'. Set TERM=xterm and stty rows/cols to match your terminal for full interactivity.
name: Upgrade to a Full TTY
description: Turn a dumb reverse shell into a fully interactive TTY so you get tab-completion, job control, and working editors/su.

steps.label: 3. Set terminal type + size on the remote

defense.why_it_works: Unix shells (bash, sh, zsh, etc.) are present by default on Linux and macOS and control every aspect of a system. Certain commands require elevated privileges, but interactive shell access provides a powerful execution environment that attackers use for commands, file operations, pivoting, and spawning further processes.
defense.prerequisites: A basic (non-interactive) shell already on the target, with python or script available.
defense.impact: A fully interactive TTY (job control, tab-completion, working sudo prompts) — improving control over the session.
defense.detection: Monitor for Unix shell execution from unexpected parent processes (e.g., a web server or database process spawning bash). Flag shell activity following unusual network connections, file writes to web directories, or privilege escalation attempts.
defense.artifacts: Spawning of python pty.spawn / script in process and command logs; network footprint unchanged (it reuses the existing shell).
defense.prevention: Use application control where appropriate to restrict which binaries can execute. On ESXi hosts, the execInstalledOnly feature prevents binaries from running unless packaged and signed as part of a vSphere installation bundle (VIB).
defense.misconfiguration: Common introductory misconfigurations: services running as root/SYSTEM unnecessarily, default credentials unchanged, unnecessary services listening on all interfaces, lack of firewall rules exposing services externally, no monitoring or alerting on authentication failures.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service listening on all interfaces with default creds (common in labs/staging):
ss -tlnp | grep LISTEN
# 0.0.0.0:21  (FTP on all interfaces)
# 0.0.0.0:3306 (MySQL on all interfaces — should be 127.0.0.1 only)
# 0.0.0.0:8080 (Tomcat with manager app accessible)

# Running services as root:
ps aux | grep -E '(mysql|apache|nginx|ftp)'
# root  1234  /usr/sbin/mysqld  <-- should run as 'mysql' user
defense.secure_config:
# Bind services to localhost or specific IPs (not 0.0.0.0):
# MySQL: my.cnf -> bind-address = 127.0.0.1
# Apache: Listen 127.0.0.1:80 (if behind a proxy)

# Run services as dedicated low-priv users:
# systemd unit: User=mysql Group=mysql

# Host-based firewall (ufw):
ufw default deny incoming
ufw allow from 10.10.1.0/24 to any port 22  # SSH from mgmt only
ufw allow 443  # HTTPS
ufw enable

# Change all default credentials immediately after installation
# Enable fail2ban for SSH and web services
